intro: Upper Mamquam Road runs east past Coast Mountain Academy toward the Mamquam area. Residents raised concerns about speeding and a high number of trucks.
The District of Squamish ranked this stretch as its top traffic calming priority. It is on the 2026 traffic calming list.

The plan has changed from speed humps. As of October 2026, the District plans two raised crosswalks and new signs on Mamquam Road east of Aristotle Drive. A raised crosswalk is a crosswalk built up like a wide, flat speed bump.
The District says the contractor expects to build the raised crosswalks on October 29 and 30, 2026, weather permitting, with single lane alternating traffic during the work.

timeline.what: Council endorsed a new Traffic Calming Policy for Squamish.
A traffic calming request was logged for Mamquam Road east of Village Drive, near Coast Mountain Academy.
The District ranked it the top priority on its traffic calming list.
The District said the raised crosswalks would be built October 29 and 30.

points: Physical changes like raised crossings slow traffic every day, not only when police are present.
Students and neighbours get safer places to cross on a road with many trucks.
Raised crossings and humps slow emergency vehicles and are hard on heavy trucks that need this road.
Some would prefer signs, enforcement or other measures that don't change the road surface.

questions.q: Is the District installing speed humps?
questions.a: No. The current plan is two raised crosswalks and updated signs.

questions.q: Will there be delays during the work?
questions.a: Yes. Expect single lane alternating traffic and minor delays on the build days.

questions.q: Can the District add more later?
questions.a: The District says sites will be monitored and more changes made if needed.
